% rhythm: article lists that open a paragraph: after a blank line an itemize, a nested itemize, a quote and a description spend \topsep and \partopsep above and below, where one inside an open paragraph spends \topsep alone
% boundary: par-list-open Birch span
% boundary: item-nested-open Cedar span
% boundary: nested-item-open Dogwood span
% boundary: list-par-open Elm span
% boundary: par-quote-open Hazel span
% boundary: quote-par-open Juniper span
% boundary: par-desc-open Larch span
% boundary: desc-item Maple span
% boundary: desc-par-open Oak span
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{fontspec}
\setmainfont{OpenSans-Regular.ttf}[Path=../corpus/fonts/, BoldFont=OpenSans-Bold.ttf, ItalicFont=OpenSans-Italic.ttf, BoldItalicFont=OpenSans-BoldItalic.ttf]
\begin{document}
Alder is the paragraph before the first list.

\begin{itemize}
\item Birch is the first item.

  \begin{itemize}
  \item Cedar opens the nested list after a blank line.
  \end{itemize}

\item Dogwood returns to the outer list.
\end{itemize}

Elm is the paragraph after the first list.

\begin{quote}
Hazel is the quoted line.
\end{quote}

Juniper is the paragraph after the quote.

\begin{description}
\item[Larch] is the first described term.
\item[Maple] is the second described term.
\end{description}

Oak closes the page.
\end{document}
